paras: The lynching of Dave Bumpers was the hanging of a Black eighteen-year-old by a mob at Athens, Georgia, in mid-December 1881. Bumpers had been accused of assaulting Mrs. Driscoll in her home, and the mob took him from the officers holding him and hanged him to an oak tree with a plow line. Northern and Southern papers carried the news as a short wire item, several under headlines that called him a "brute" or a "miscreant."

According to the dispatch, Bumpers entered Mrs. Driscoll's home in Athens on a Monday night while her husband was away and assaulted her "in a brutal manner." The accusation appears only in this one account, which stated it as fact.

Bumpers was captured on the following Friday night while asleep in a cotton house. The dispatch says he was then "tried and sent to jail," without saying before what court or with what result. A mob then took him from "the officers who had him in charge" and hanged him to an oak tree with a plow line "till he was dead."

The dispatch does not give the hour, the size of the mob, the place of the tree, or the names of anyone involved. Because it was datelined Athens, December 17, and placed the capture "last night," the hanging most likely took place on December 16 or 17.
No report of an inquest, arrest or official response appears in the coverage.

The story reached the press as one brief wire dispatch, datelined Athens, December 17, in the Portland Daily Press and Atlanta, December 18, in the New Haven Morning Journal and Courier, both on December 19. The New Haven paper headed it "A Colored Brute's Fate" and the Portland paper "Swift Punishment for a Miscreant," framing the hanging as a deserved penalty for a crime the dispatch treated as proven.

Over the next week the same text ran in Wilmington, Delaware, as "Hanged With a Plow-Line," in Ridgway, Pennsylvania, as "By the Plew-Line," and in a "Southern News" column in Stephens City, Virginia. The Delaware version left out the words "had him in charge and," so that it read as if the officers themselves had hanged him. No paper added comment, local detail or a follow-up, and no Georgia paper's account appears in the coverage.

bases: Every report says a mob took Bumpers, held on an assault accusation, from the officers and hanged him until he was dead [A1, A2].

accounts.gist: Bumpers assaulted Mrs. Driscoll on Monday night, was captured Friday night asleep in a cotton house, was tried and jailed, and was taken from the officers by a mob and hanged to an oak tree with a plow line.

framing.detail: Headlines 'A Colored Brute's Fate' and 'Swift Punishment for a Miscreant' state the accusation as fact and present the hanging as deserved punishment.
Delaware, Pennsylvania and Virginia papers ran the same text under 'Hanged With a Plow-Line', 'By the Plew-Line' or in a news column, without comment.
